correctness.rationale: Proof steps: tangent cones give exact Gaussian section formulas (1),(2); interior projection gives strictly nested sets of positive Gaussian measure; dominated convergence gives endpoint limits; finite minimum and intermediate value theorem give a single crossing and strict global maximum; continuous parameter dependence and regular-base edge equality follow. Executed standalone 3D numerical checks of 1,200 angles. The sampling is not relied on for the all-dimensional proof.

evidence: Akopyan--Karasev 2015 prove the regular tetrahedron upper bound in dimension three; their Conjecture 2.1 for all dimensions is not proved.

The present theorem treats one-parameter variations over every fixed full-dimensional polytopal base and every fixed interior projection; the regular-base case gives the unique maximizing height in every dimension.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An unrestricted regular-simplex upper bound, when known in dimension three, implies at most an upper bound for a special regular-base family, not monotone angular behavior or unique balancing for arbitrary fixed bases. In higher dimensions the paper explicitly treats the broader conjecture as unproved.

value.rationale: Solves a natural sharp max-min solid-angle objective with an exact unique optimizer for all dimensions and arbitrary polytopal bases, not just a special case or table. The theorem identifies the geometric mechanism (opposing strict angle monotonicities), makes the optimum constructible by scalar bisection, proves continuous dependence on apex projection, and yields the regular-simplex benchmark from the same universal principle.
